testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Verify pen is not paired to device.
2. Press and hold the tail button for 5+ seconds.
Verify: The pairing LED blinks slowly (Pairing Mode).

1. Go to Settings -> Devices -> Bluetooth and other devices.
2. Select 'Add Bluetooth or other device'.
3. Select Bluetooth.
4. Select the pen to pair.
Verify: The pen pairs.

testCases.testName: Bluetooth and Other Devices - Battery Percentages

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Pen paired.
Verify: Battery is displayed with connected pen.

1. Use a pen that is already paired to the device. 
2. Press and hold the tail button for 5 seconds.
Verify: Pairing mode not entered (LED does not continuously blink slowly)
1. Connect 2 pens to the same host.\n2. Click the tail button of each pen.\nVerify: Both pens open default application. (Settings\Devices\Pen & Windows Ink\Pen shortcuts)

1. Pair a pen to the host.
2. Go to Settings -> Devices -> Bluetooth and other devices.
3. Select the Surface Pen under "Mouse, Keyboard, Pen".
4. Select Remove Device.
Verify: The pen is removed.
5. Press the pen tail button.
Verify: Inkspace does Not Open.

1. Remove pen via Bluetooth menu.
2. win+R to open Run and enter:  ms-surface-app:penfuse?reset
3. Touch pen tip to screen.
Verify: First Run Experience launches.

During the OOBE setup
I. During the OOBE, you'll be using the Pen next.
II. Another screen will come up.
III. Use your Pen and tap on an action button on the screen to follow the prompt.
IV. Verify using Pen capabilities during OOBE setup responds correctly.
(Pen pairing is not required during this step)

After wake from sleep.
Verify: keyboard and touchpad functionality and that pen is still paired and charging in dock.

After wake from hibernate.
Verify: keyboard and touchpad functionality and that pen is still paired and charging in dock.

After system restart.
Verify: keyboard and touchpad functionality and that pen is still paired and charging in dock.

After system bootup.
Verify: keyboard and touchpad functionality and that pen is still paired and charging in dock.

Verify: Pen is not paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings -> Bluetooth Pen -> Remove device.)

2. Tap and drag on locked screen with pen tip.

testCases.testName: Screen Locked - No Pairing via WLC blade dock

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Verify: Pen is not paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings -> Bluetooth Pen -> Remove device.)
1. Lock screen. (Start Menu -> Account symbol -> Lock. Or Win+L)
2. Dock pen in keyboard WLC pocket. Wait 5 seconds.
3. Remove pen from keyboard pocket.
4. Unlock screen.
Verify: Pen is still not paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings -> Bluetooth Pen.)

testCases.testName: Pen WLC Blade Docked - Tail Button

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Verify: Pen is paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings.)
1. Single tail button press. Verify Whiteboard or chosen application opens.
2. Dock Pen. (Place in keyboard's WLC pen pocket.)
3. Single tail button press while docked.
Verify: Application does not open while pen is docked.

testCases.testName: Screen Locked -  No Pairing via built in charger

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Verify: Pen is not paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings -> Bluetooth Pen -> Remove device.)
1. Lock screen. (Start Menu -> Account symbol -> Lock. Or Win+L)
2. Dock pen to built in charger. Wait 5 seconds.
3. Remove pen from built in charger.
4. Unlock screen.
Verify: Pen is still not paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings -> Bluetooth Pen.)

testCases.testName: Pen built in charger - Loose Coupling

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Verify: Pen is not paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings -> Bluetooth Pen -> Remove device.)
2. Dock pen to built in charger. Wait 10 seconds.
3. Remove pen from built in charger.
Verify: Pen has paired to the device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings -> Bluetooth Pen.)

testCases.testName: Pen built in charger Docked - Charging

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Verify: Pen is paired to host device and note battery % of pen (must be less than 100%). (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings.)
1. Dock Pen to built in charger.
2. Wait 3-5 minutes.
3. Remove pen from charging base, tail button to wake and refresh battery %.
Verify: Pen battery % increased.

testCases.testName: Pen built in charger Docked - Tail Button

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
Verify: Pen is paired to host device. (Settings -> Bluetooth and other device settings.)
1. Single tail button press. Verify Whiteboard or chosen application opens.
2. Dock Pen to built in charger.
3. Single tail button press while docked.
Verify: Application does not open while pen is docked.

testCases.testName: Pen Docked USB-C charging base - Charging

testScenarios.detailedSteps:

testCases.testName: Surface App - Pen Pressure - Ballpoint Pen Tool

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Open Surface App.
2. Select Pen Tab -> ballpoint pen tool and draw a line in the test area.
3. Set pressure sensitivity slider to Light and draw in the test area.
Verify: Lines drawn are thiner than the first line drawn, and become thicker with more pressure applied while drawing.
4. Set Presure sensitivity slider to Heavy and draw in the test area
Verify: Lines drawn are thicker than the first line drawn.

testCases.testName: Surface App - Pen Pressure - Pencil Tool

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Open Surface App.
2. Select Pen Tab -> pencil tool and draw a line in the test area.
3. Set pressure sensitivity slider to Light and draw in the test area.
Verify: Lines drawn are thiner than the first line drawn, and become darker with more pressure applied while drawing.
4. Set Presure sensitivity slider to Heavy and draw in the test area
Verify: Lines drawn are darker than the first line drawn.

1. Open Surface App.
2. Select Pen Tab.
3. Draw in test area many parrallel lines in quick succession.
Verify: No missed or connected lines.

1. Open Surface App.
2. Select Pen Tab.
3. Draw in test area with force then hover over test area with pen.
Verify: No inking while hovering.

1. Open Surface App.
2. Select pen tab.
3. Draw several lines in test area.
4. Erase the lines using the tail one line at a time.
Verify: The eraser is precise and can erase single lines at a time.

testCases.testName: Surface App - Erase with screen pressure and not from hovering

testScenarios.detailedSteps:
1. Open Surface App.
2. Select pen tab.
3. Draw several lines in test area.
4. Erase some of the lines using pressure on screen.
5. Hover the eraser and move around drawing area.
Verify: The eraser does not erase remaining lines while hovering.

4. Draw some more lines in Snip & Sketch.

Draw near the bottom, sides and top edges of the windowed app.\nVerify: The ink is where it is supposed to be. No lines going off edge or other anomolies.
